Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:69: Further they said in the Pesikta (D'Rav Kahana, section 24): I accepted the repentance of Ahab, but I will not accept your repentance - for a harsh decree was decreed against him, this is what is written (1 Kings 21:17-19), "and the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying... go down to meet Ahab," and so on, "thus says the LORD of hosts, in the place where the dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick your blood, even yours." "And it came to pass, when Ahab heard these words, that he tore his clothes," and so on, "and went softly" - what is "went softly"? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, he walked barefoot. What is written there (ibid. 21:29)? "Have you seen how Ahab humbles himself before Me? Because he humbles himself before Me, I will not bring the evil in his days."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:70: I accepted the repentance of the men of Anathoth, but I will not accept your repentance - for a harsh decree was decreed against them, as it is written (Jeremiah 11:22), "thus says the LORD, behold, I will punish them," and so on, "and there shall be no remnant of them" - and yet, since they repented, they merited to be listed in genealogy, as explained in Ezra (Nehemiah 11:32).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:71: I accepted the repentance of the men of Nineveh, but I will not accept your repentance - for a harsh decree was decreed against them, as it is written (Jonah 3:4-5), "and Jonah began to enter into the city," and so on, "and the people of Nineveh believed God," and it is written, "who knows, God may turn and repent." I accepted the repentance of Yechonyah, but I will not accept your repentance - for a harsh decree was decreed against him, as it is written (Jeremiah 22:28), "is this man Coniah a despised, broken vessel?"
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:72: And in Vayikra Rabbah, parashah 10, they said, in these words: Rav Acha and Rabbi Avin bar Binyamin in the name of Rabbi Abba: great is the power of repentance, for it nullifies the decree and nullifies the oath. The oath, as it is written (Jeremiah 22:24), "as I live, says the LORD, though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon My right hand." And it nullifies the decree, "thus says the LORD, write this man childless" (ibid. 22:30), and it is written (1 Chronicles 3:17), "and the sons of Jeconiah, Assir; Shealtiel his son" - "Assir" [prisoner] - because he was bound in the prison house; "Shealtiel his son" - for from him the kingdom of the House of David was replanted. Rabbi Tanchum bar Yirmiyah said: "Assir" - this is the Holy One, blessed be He, who bound Himself with an oath; "Shealtiel" - that He inquired [sha'al El] of the heavenly court concerning His vow - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:73: And so they said in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, page 106a, in the Sabba) concerning this Yechonyah, that repentance nullified the oath and the decree, in these words: the place from which the Master of repentance ascends - even perfectly righteous men cannot stand there - and therefore, once he has returned in repentance, the Holy One, blessed be He, certainly accepts him at once. We have learned, there is no word in the world that stands before repentance, and to everyone the Holy One, blessed be He, certainly accepts - and if he returns in repentance, behold, the path of life is ready to receive him; even though he blemished whatever he blemished, everything is repaired and everything returns to its repair - for even concerning what there is an oath before the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is called "God of hosts," it is written, "I have purposed, and who shall annul it?" - this is a concealed secret.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:74: And further, when the Holy One, blessed be He, swears an oath, He swears only conditionally, unless [the person] performs repentance - for there is no word that stands before repentance, and for everything the Holy One, blessed be He, atones; when they perform complete repentance, the Holy One, blessed be He, accepts, as it is written, "as I live, says the LORD, though Coniah," and so on, and it is written, "write this man childless" - and after he returned in repentance, it is written, "and the sons of Coniah, Assir [Shealtiel] his son" - from here, that repentance breaks several decrees and judgments and several chains of iron, and there is none who stands before repentance. And concerning this it is written (Isaiah 66:24), "and they shall go forth and look upon the corpses of the men who have transgressed against Me" - it does not say "who transgressed against Me" [in past tense alone] but "the ones transgressing against Me" [in an ongoing sense] - meaning, those who did not wish to return in repentance and be comforted for what they did; but once they are comforted, behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, accepts them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:75: Therefore, a person, even though he transgressed against Him and blemished in a place where it was not necessary, and returns before Him, He accepts him and has compassion on him - for the Holy One, blessed be He, is full of mercy toward him, and filled with mercy over all His works, as it says (Psalms 145:9), "and His mercies are over all His works," and even over beasts and birds His mercies extend - if His mercies extend to them, all the more so to people who know and recognize their Master, that His mercies extend to them and rest upon them. And concerning this David said (ibid. 119:156), "great are Your mercies, O LORD; revive me according to Your judgments" - if His mercies extend to the wicked, all the more so to the righteous. Rather, who needs healing? Those who have the ailment. And who are those with the ailment? These are the wicked - they need healing and mercy, and the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on them, that they not be abandoned by Him, and He does not depart from them, so that they return to Him. When the Holy One, blessed be He, draws near with the right, He draws near; and when He pushes away with the left, He pushes away; and at the time His right pushes away, He draws near - from this side He pushes away, and from that side He draws near, and the Holy One, blessed be He, never withholds mercy from them. Come and see what is written (Isaiah 57:17), "and he went on backsliding in the way of his heart" - and it is written after it, "I have seen his ways, and will heal him; I will also lead him, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners." "And he went on backsliding" - even though the wicked do what they do in willful defiance, walking in the way of their own heart, warnings are given to them and they do not wish to heed them - at the time they return in repentance and take the good path of repentance, behold, healing is ready to receive them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:76: Now one must consider whether the verse speaks of the living or of the dead - for the beginning of the verse is not the same as its end, nor the end the same as the beginning; the beginning of the verse points to the living, and its end points to the dead. Rather, the verse means: while a person is in his life, and thus, "he went on backsliding in the way of his heart" - because the evil inclination that is in him strengthens itself against him, and therefore he goes on backsliding and does not wish to return in repentance - the Holy One, blessed be He, sees his ways going in evil without benefit, and the Holy One, blessed be He, says, I must strengthen him with My hand. This is what is written, "I have seen his ways, and will heal him" - that they go in darkness, I wish to give him healing. "And will heal him" - the Holy One, blessed be He, brings into his heart the ways of repentance and healing for his soul. "I will also lead him" - along the lines of (Exodus 32:34), "go, lead the people" - the Holy One, blessed be He, guides him on a straight path, like one who grasps another's hand and brings him out of the darkness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:77: "And restore comforts to him and to his mourners" - behold, it appears that he is dead - but certainly he is [called] dead while alive, for since he is wicked he is called dead. What is "and restore comforts to him and to his mourners"? Rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, does good with people, and once a person enters from the age of thirteen years onward, He appoints two guardian angels with him - to this point. And the rest of his words we copied in the Gate of Fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:78: And although we have elaborated in copying this discourse, it is because of its abundant benefit for repentance, for its words subdue the heart, and from it you see how great is the virtue of repentance, and how great is the mercy of the LORD upon His creatures, to bring into their hearts the ways of repentance and to raise them from darkness to light and from death to life. And through this the penitent will be aroused to repent out of love - for since the Holy One, blessed be He, in His love for him, brought repentance into his heart, or set before him the ways of repentance, then it is fitting that he love Him and do His will - and so the pious one wrote in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Love, chapter 2), that one of the things that arouse love is when one considers the kindness of God toward him, in being patient with his transgressions, and in forgiving him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:79: And so they expounded in Midrash Rabbah (parashah 10), in these words: "his palate is sweetness" - this is the Holy One, blessed be He. See what He says (Amos 5:4), "for thus says the LORD to the house of Israel, seek Me, and live" - and you have a sweeter palate than this (Ezekiel 33:11), "as I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked," and so on - and you have something sweeter than this, "but that the wicked turn," and so on. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, but only if he regrets the wicked deed [in the past]. How so? Rashbi, peace be upon him, taught: behold, one who was a completely wicked person all his days, and at the end became a completely righteous person - of him it is said, "and the wickedness of the wicked shall not make him stumble." Rabbi Yochanan said, and not only that, but all the transgressions he committed, the Holy One, blessed be He, counts them for him as merits - this is what is written (Psalms 45:9), "myrrh, aloes, and cassia are all your garments" - "all your betrayals" that you betrayed against Me are like myrrh and aloes, when they are the "cassia" of betrayals - and it says of them, he shall live - to this point. And without doubt this matter, that iniquities are counted as merits, applies to one who repents out of love, as explained in Tractate Yoma (86b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:80: Further, among those who repented and were accepted is Menasheh son of Chizkiyahu. It is said in Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer (chapter 42): Rabbi Yehoshua says, know the power of repentance - come and see from Menasheh son of Chizkiyahu, who committed every evil abomination in the world and did much evil in the world, and sacrificed to other gods, as it is said (2 Chronicles 33:6), "and he made his children pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom," and so on, "and did much evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke Him" - and he went out to Jerusalem flying doves and sacrificing to all the host of heaven, and the captains of the armies of Assyria came and seized him with a hook through his nose, brought him down to Babylon, and placed him in a copper vessel of fire; and there he called to all the other gods to whom he had sacrificed, and none of them called to him or answered him or saved him. He said, I will call to the God of my fathers with all my heart - perhaps the LORD will do for me according to all His wonders. And when he called to the God of his fathers, He was entreated by him and heard his prayer, as it is said (2 Chronicles 33:13), "and he prayed to Him, and He was entreated by him" - at that hour Menasheh said, there is judgment and there is a Judge.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:81: Further, in Midrash Rut (5:6), in these words: another interpretation, "come here" speaks of Menasheh - "come here" - draw near to the kingdom. "And eat of the bread" - this is the bread of kingship. "And dip your morsel in the vinegar" - for he soiled his deeds like vinegar, from his evil deeds. "And she sat beside the reapers" - for his kingdom was hunted [as prey] for a time, as it is written (2 Chronicles 33:10), "and the LORD spoke to Menasheh and to his people, but they would not listen; therefore the LORD brought upon them the captains of the army of the king of Assyria, who took Menasheh among the thorns" [with hooks]. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said, like a Domnican [device]; Rabbi Levi bar Chaita said, they made for him a copper cage, kindling fire beneath it, and he cried out, "idol of so-and-so, save me! Idol of so-and-so, save me!" When he saw that they did not help him, he said, I remember my father used to read to me, "when you are in distress, and all these things come upon you," and so on, "for the LORD your God is a merciful God" - I will cry out to Him; if He answers, good; and if not, well, all mouths are the same [it can't hurt to try]. At that hour the ministering angels arose and stopped up all the windows above, and said before Him, Master of the universe, a man who set up an idol in the Sanctuary - You accept him in repentance? He said to them, if I do not accept him in repentance, I lock the door in the face of all penitents. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He dug a tunnel for him beneath the Throne of Glory, from a place over which no angel has power - this is what is written (2 Chronicles 33:13), "and he prayed to Him, and He was entreated by him, and heard his supplication." Rabbi Levi said, in Arabic they call a tunnel "atirah" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:82: Further, they said in the Sifrei (Deuteronomy 3:29), "and we dwelt in the valley opposite Beit Peor" - Moses said to Israel: see what sin I committed [at Meribah], and how many requests I made, yet I was not forgiven - see the sin you committed [at Peor], yet the Holy One, blessed be He, says to you, repent, and I will accept. Rabbi Yehuda says, this teaches that in several places Israel came to a grave sin, and the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, repent, and I will accept, as it is said (ibid. 4:1), "and now, Israel, hearken to the statutes and to the judgments," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:83: Further they said in Vayikra Rabbah on "and this is the law of the guilt-offering": thus said the Holy One, blessed be He, to Israel: My children, it is I who said to you, I desire only joyous song, and one in whom there is no transgression - I retract My words: even if a person commits several transgressions, one worse than another, and returns in repentance, and humbles himself like the earth, and views himself as though half innocent and half liable, bringing a suspended guilt-offering every day - behold, I am with him in mercy, and I accept him in repentance, and give him male children who occupy themselves with Torah and commandments and keep the words of Torah in their mouths, as it is said (Isaiah 53:10), "yet it pleased the LORD to crush him, He has put him to grief; when You make his soul a guilt-offering, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:84: And since the virtue of repentance is so great, to atone for what a person has done, as explained in the previous discourses, it is not fitting that a person be negligent in repenting - for His right hand is stretched out to receive penitents, and the door is always open, and whoever does not repent, his punishment is great in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:85: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, gave a fitting parable concerning this matter in Midrash Kohelet (Midrash Zuta, chapter 7), on the verse (Job 11:20), "but the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall have no way to flee." They said: a parable of a band of robbers who rebelled against the king; he caught them and imprisoned them in the prison house. What did they do? They dug a single tunnel and escaped through it. There was one among them who did not flee; in the morning the king found him and said to him, fool, the tunnel is before you and you did not flee? So the Holy One, blessed be He, said to the wicked: repentance is before you, and you do not return - this is what is written, "and they shall have no way to flee" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:86: And know that this tunnel to which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, gave this parable is the small opening in the letter heh - as we say in Menachot (29b): why was this world created with a heh? Because it resembles a portico, in that whoever wishes to leave may leave. What is the reason its leg [of the heh] is suspended [detached]? Because if he returns in repentance, he is brought back in through it. And why not let him enter through the same opening he left by? Because it does not work out that way - as Reish Lakish said: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said, what is the meaning of (Proverbs 3:34), "surely He scoffs at the scoffers, but gives grace to the lowly"? One who comes to defile himself, they open [the way] for him; one who comes to purify himself, they assist him. Why is there a crown-like flourish on it [the yud in the heh]? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: if he returns, I will tie for him a crown like My own - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:87: It follows that his entering through the narrow supernal opening is so that he be hidden from the masters of judgment - and so they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 62, page 94b), that through repentance one is hidden from the masters of judgment, in these words: further, "and I saw that I was naked, and I hid myself" (Genesis 3:8-10) - and through what is a person hidden from these judgments, that they not rule over him? Through repentance - this is what is written (Psalms 91:1), "he who dwells in the secret place of the Most High" - this is the Mother, who is the secret of the Most High, from Chochmah, which is known only through her - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:88: And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in Pesachim (119a), "and the hands of a man were under their wings" (Ezekiel 1:8) - Rav Kahana said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosi, and the Rabbis said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda the Prince: these are the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He, spread out beneath the wings of the Chayot, to receive penitents from before the attribute of judgment - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:89: And having spoken of the awakenings to repentance and its virtue, let us speak of the nature of repentance:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:1: In explaining the nature of repentance, the pious one in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Repentance, chapter 1) explained that the nature of repentance is a person's restoration to the service of the Creator, blessed be He, after his departure from it and his sinning within it. And departure from the service of the Creator is of two kinds: either by abandoning what the Creator commanded to do and neglecting it, or by doing what He warned against doing, intending thereby to rebel against his Creator.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:2: And if his departure from service is of the first kind - abandoning what he was commanded - the manner of his repentance is that he hasten and increase, from now on, in commandments, Torah, and the like. And if he transgressed the command, his repentance is that that man distance himself to the far extreme, until he returns to the middle line. And the parable for this is a person whose body has become ill because of food - whether because he refrained from eating what would maintain his health, or because he ate what harmed him and impaired his health. For the first case, his remedy is to increase for himself the kinds of foods proper to his nature; and if his illness was because he ate what harmed him, his remedy is to guard himself from that food and to conduct himself in the opposite of his [prior] disposition, until he returns to the state of balance - to this point is the summary of his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:3: And according to the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in the Zohar and the Tikkunim, according to the nature of the blemish shall be the repentance. We have already explained in the Gate of Fear that the sinner causes the departure of the supernal Mother from over the children, or the departure of the lower Mother from over the lower worlds - and all according to the greatness of the blemish, so it causes the departure - and the intent in the word "teshuvah" [repentance] is the return of the levels and their repair to their original state.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:4: And the parable is a channel of water flowing from a spring, and that water goes to water several gardens, orchards, fields, and vineyards - and someone comes, in his folly, and diverts the water channel to a garbage heap, an empty place with no benefit; the owner of the spring will be angry with him for two reasons - one, that he stopped watering his good gardens, and the second, that he damaged and broke the pipe.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:5: And the thing illustrated is more severe in its punishment than the parable - for the sinner, besides having damaged the pipes of the flow from reaching their proper place, directs them to a place that angers the King, the LORD of hosts - namely, that he brings forth holiness into impurity, a place that should be dry and desolate, and he waters and saturates it. And this matter is found especially concerning forbidden relations, when one comes to a gentile woman, and likewise one who emits seed in vain, and similarly with the blemish of the tongue - for blemishing the covenant of the tongue is more severe than the covenant of the organ.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:6: And the manner of repentance is to repair the broken pipes and return the flow to its place, to each and every place according to where the blemish was. If the blemish was in the supernal Mother, causing "Ra Y-H, Ra Y-H" [evil inserted between the letters yud-heh], having introduced evil between the letters yud-heh, he shall cause, through repentance, the unification of the letters yud-heh and the removal of the evil - and through this the Mother returns to the children. And if the blemish was in forbidden relations, "Ra V-H" [evil inserted between vav-heh], having introduced "ra" between vav and heh - through which the Mother is exiled from her place and a maidservant inherits her mistress - his repentance is to remove that evil from there and to unify the vav with the heh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:7: And all this is called "teshuvah" [repentance/return]: "tashuv heh" - the supernal heh returns over the children, and the heh returns to the yud; and likewise the lower "heh" returns over the lower worlds, and the heh returns to unite with the vav. And this introduction is briefly alluded to in the Tikkunim, and is [explained] at length in other places in the Zohar; in these words, in Tikkun 63 (page 94b), he says there, on the verse (Psalms 1:1), "happy is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked" - and he explained that "asher" [who] is the Mother [Imma], "asher hotzeticha me-eretz Mitzrayim" [who brought you out of the land of Egypt] - certainly she is repentance, the healing of all illnesses and afflictions - this is what is written (Lamentations 2:13), "who can heal you?" - and of her it is said (Isaiah 6:10), "and return, and be healed," "it shall be healing to your navel" (Proverbs 3:8) - happy is he who returns to his own husband; it is the secret of repentance, that returns that level that had been distanced from its place, returning it to its place and bringing it near there. At the time the Shechinah is distanced from her husband, it is said of a person (Deuteronomy 28:66), "and your life shall hang in doubt before you" - "your life" is so called, this is what is written (Genesis 2:7), "and He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life," at the time he brings her near to her husband - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:8: And so he also explained in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, end of page 106) - they said there on the verse (Isaiah 57:18), "and restore comforts to him and to his mourners" - that when a person sins, the angels that accompany him withdraw from him and mourn over him, and when he returns in repentance, they are comforted; they said, of blessed memory: and now that they have returned to him, this is certainly comfort on every side, and now he is alive - certainly alive on every side, holding fast to the Tree of Life - and since he holds fast to the Tree of Life, certainly then he is called "ba'al teshuvah" [master/possessor of repentance/return] - for the Community of Israel is also called "teshuvah," and he is her "ba'al" [husband/master] - and the ancients said, "ba'al teshuvah" literally. And therefore even completely righteous men cannot stand in his place - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:9: Behold, in this discourse the matter of two [kinds of] repentance is explained: what he explained, that the ancients said "ba'al teshuvah" literally, is the supernal repentance - and since he is literally "ba'al teshuvah," certainly he also ascends to the place of the yud, where the secret of life is, which is the place of union - and this is "alive, holding fast on every side." And there is a secret in this that is not the place for it here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:10: It is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 15b), the matter of these two repentances, and incidentally is explained how great the blemish is in them, and according to the blemish is the repentance required. In these words: Rabbi Yosi said, it is written (Leviticus 18:7), "the nakedness of your father, and the nakedness of your mother, you shall not uncover," and it is written, "she is your mother, you shall not uncover her nakedness" - "she is your mother" certainly - so if he has uncovered her nakedness, for whom must he repair it? Certainly for the one who uncovered it - for we have learned, when the evil inclination grows great in a person, it happens only through those forbidden relations, and all sins are bound up in that "nakedness," and it is written, "you shall not uncover" - when it is repaired, it is repaired corresponding to the one who uncovered - and this is called "teshuvah" [repentance].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:11: Rabbi Yitzchak said: all the sins of the world are bound one to another, until the Mother is uncovered among them; and when she is uncovered, all those children are uncovered because of her - and it is written (Deuteronomy 22:6), "you shall not take the mother with the sons." And when the world is repaired below, everything is repaired, until the repair rises to the holy Mother to be repaired, and she is covered again from what was uncovered - and therefore (Psalms 32:1), "happy is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered" - and then it is called "teshuvah," repentance indeed, and then the Day of Atonement is called, as it is written (Leviticus 16:30), "from all your sins before the LORD you shall be pure."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:12: Behold, Rabbi Yosi explained repentance concerning the lower Mother, and Rabbi Yitzchak explained repentance concerning the supernal Mother, who is called the Day of Atonement. But one must understand, according to both opinions, what is the matter of the "uncovering." But it is possible to say that the created world is her garment, and one who blemishes the throne uncovers her from her garment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:13: And so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 23a); they said: certainly now we hear what we had not heard until now - that certainly the Holy One, blessed be He, created nothing that He did not need, and moreover, the Torah of creation is the garment of the Shechinah. Had Adam not been destined to be created, the Shechinah would have been without covering, like a poor person - and therefore, whoever sins, it is as though he stripped the Shechinah of her garment, and this is Adam's punishment. And whoever fulfills a commandment of the Torah, it is as though he clothed the Shechinah in her garment - and therefore they established, concerning the covering of tzitzit and tefillin (Exodus 22:26), "for it alone is his covering, it is his garment for his skin; wherein shall he sleep" in exile? - and this has already been established - to this point. And above this, the matter is explained more fully, and to avoid lengthening we have not copied all his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:14: And so the garment of the supernal Mother is the six extremities, in which she is clothed - and when there is a blemish in them, she is found uncovered, and repentance is to repair the lower attributes in which she is covered - and then it is the repentance in which she returns over the children.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:15: Further, they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayikra, page 16a) that repentance ascends up to Keter, in these words: we have learned, at the time deeds below become fit and the Mother is in gladness, the Holy Ancient One is revealed and light returns to Ze'ir Anpin, and then all is in gladness, all is in completeness, all is found in blessings, and mercy is ready, and all the worlds are in gladness - this is what is written (Micah 7:19), "He will return [yashuv], He will have compassion on us; He will subdue our iniquities" - who is "yashuv"? The Holy Ancient One returns to be revealed in the small [Ze'ir Anpin]; He returns, returns, to be revealed, having been concealed at first - and all this is called "teshuvah." Rabbi Yehuda said, all is in general, all is undefined, as it is written (Deuteronomy 13:18), "that the LORD may turn from the fierceness of His anger, and show you mercy" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:16: Behold, it is explicit that he said, "who is 'yashuv'? The Holy Ancient One." And according to Rabbi Yehuda, the whole of Atzilut, up to above Keter, is all called "teshuvah" - and this is "yashuv YHVH," namely the unification of the Name in its letters through the Cause of causes - and through this, "and show you mercy."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:17: Further, there, further on, concerning (Leviticus 5:23), "then he shall restore [ve-heishiv] the theft which he has stolen" - he says: one who wishes to repair his deeds as we have said - "and he shall restore" - who does the restoring? Rather, it is like one who repairs his deeds in order that the wellsprings of water return to their places, to water the plantings - for through his sins he has caused them to be withheld from them, and therefore "he shall restore the theft," as explained - to this point. And the intent of the author of the discourse is that it was difficult for him that the verse should have said "and it shall return [ve-yashuv] the theft," since the word "ve-heishiv" is in the causative form (Hif'il) - but according to his explanation it is resolved, for through the repair of his deeds, he causes the supernal blessings that had been stolen from their place and source to return to their place - it follows that he performs, above, a novel act through the repair of his deeds.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:18: Further, further on, at the end of the aforementioned page: happy is the portion of the masters of repentance, and happy is the portion of the righteous, for whose sake the world endures - this is what is written (Leviticus 5:23), "and it shall be, when he has sinned and is guilty," and so on. What is written above? "Or has found what was lost, and lies concerning it," and so on - for because of this the Holy One, blessed be He, is removed from everything - as it were, the Holy One, blessed be He, is not found in His stability, for the Community of Israel is separated from her place - this is what is written (Jeremiah 7:28), "faithfulness [emunah] has perished" - what is "emunah"? This is the Community of Israel, along the lines of (Psalms 92:3), "and Your faithfulness in the nights." "Why has the land perished" (Jeremiah 9:11)? And all is one, and it has already been established, "perished," not "was lost" [ne'evedet] and not "lost" [avudah] - along these lines, "the righteous has perished" (Isaiah 57:1) - "avud" or "ne'evad" is not written, but "avad" - this is what is written, "faithfulness has perished." Therefore, "he shall restore the theft or the lost thing" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 2:19: And the intent in their saying "found what was lost" is that the Shechinah is called "lost" when she loses the supernal blessings because of the blemish of the lower ones - and along these lines, "the righteous has perished," which they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, end of page 55) as "all those blessings have perished." And in the Tikkunim, Tikkun 11 (page 26b), they explained "avad" as "avad la-Matronita" [perished for the Matronita], and of her it is said (Isaiah 19:5), "and the river shall be wasted and dried up." And this is because when the Matronita is not in her place, the blessings depart from the Righteous One [Yesod, called "Tzaddik"]. And what he said concerning "faithfulness has perished" - the meaning is that the attribute called "faithfulness," which indicates the blessings, has perished. Up to "why has the land perished" - for the attribute of "Eretz" [land, i.e., Malchut] has lost the blessings - and it all comes to the same point. And along these lines they also explained in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, page 266b).
